newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details primary elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details primary elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Primary elevator space tightened slightly in the past week across the Canadian Prairies, Canadian Wheat Board said.
"Primary elevator space tightened somewhat over the past week, averaging 25 percent across the Prairies," the CWB statement said.
Elevators in Alberta and Saskatchewan averaged 26 percent of space vacant while Manitoba was the tightest for space at 21 percent vacant.
Railcar unloads at export positions fell below their targetted allocations, it said.
Vancouver unloads totaled 1,717 hopper cars, below the 3,400 target. Prince Rupert unloads reached 670 compared to the target of 1,500. Thunder Bay unloads reached 294 compared to the target of 620.
"The CWB met with railways, terminal operators and labour groups last week to discuss the lineup of ships at Canadian ports. No long-term solutions were reached to break the backlog," it said.
There were 34 ships waiting at the West coast ans six waiting on the East coast at the time the CWB statement was issued, CWB said.
